answers.answer: fzf is a general-purpose command-line fuzzy finder and interactive terminal toolkit. It reads candidate text from stdin (or obtains file candidates without a pipe), lets users select matches, and writes selections to stdout. Shell users, pipelines/scripts, bundled shell key bindings/completion, and Vim/Neovim integrations run it. The noninteractive filter mode serves scripts. External integrations are consumers, not all part of this repository; fzf.vim is explicitly a separate project.

main.go owns CLI startup and special output modes. src/options.go parses configuration; src/core.go Run coordinates execution. Reader ingests channels, commands, files, or stdin. ChunkList holds items; Pattern builds queries and matches items; Matcher scans chunks and produces merged results. Terminal handles interactive input/output; src/tui supplies terminal event/color primitives. src/algo provides fuzzy/exact algorithms; src/util supplies shared infrastructure such as EventBox. src/protector provides OS-specific startup protection. shell/ supplies shell integration.

The executable and core are Go, organized by one module github.com/junegunn/fzf (go 1.23.0). Package main imports package fzf at /src plus /src/protector; /src/algo, /src/tui, and /src/util are distinct internal Go package boundaries, not separate services. Go modules pin dependencies including tcell/v2, fastwalk, go-shellwords and x/term. Make drives architecture-specific go build, Go tests, and GoReleaser builds/releases. Ruby/Bundler/Minitest supply executable integration tests, with tmux for interactive tests. Shell scripts supply integration; Vim integration is documented separately. The map reports limited language extraction for Ruby, shell and gomod, so it does not establish their full call graphs.

The selected executable begins at package main's main() in main.go:58. It invokes protector.Protect(), then fzf.ParseOptions(true, os.Args[1:]). After handling script/help/version/man branches, normal execution calls fzf.Run(options) at line 113 and passes its result to exit, which calls os.Exit. Run is defined in src/core.go:55.

Noninteractive filtering is the opts.Filter != nil branch inside fzf.Run in src/core.go (Run definition at line 55; filtering around 259-352). Streaming mode calls Pattern.MatchItem; buffered mode calls Matcher.scan, which searches chunks through Pattern.Match. It is not a separate filter executable or Terminal method.

main.go directly depends on github.com/junegunn/fzf/src (aliased fzf) and /src/protector: imports at lines 10-11 prove package direction. Uses include fzf.ParseOptions (60), Usage, ExitError, WriteTemporaryFile (98), and Run (113); protector.Protect is called at startup. The map independently resolves main→ParseOptions/Run/WriteTemporaryFile. Protect's implementation is build-tag selected: OpenBSD pledges; other platforms use a no-op. Reader, Matcher, Pattern, tui and util are not direct imports of main.go. Embedded shell scripts/manpage are direct resource dependencies (go:embed), not Go function calls.

Assuming ordinary defaults: shell pipe → main → ParseOptions (--filter stores foo; --no-sort sets Sort=0) → Run. Filter/non-sort/non-tac/non-sync/non-benchmark selects streaming. Run builds a Pattern and installs a NewReader callback. Reader.ReadSource sees non-tty stdin → readFromStdin → feed(os.Stdin) → newline records → pusher callback → item transformation → Pattern.MatchItem. Default extended matching dispatches extendedMatch→iter→the term's algorithm function (default FuzzyMatchV2). Successful items go through transformer→Printer (default fmt.Println); Run returns success if any match, otherwise no-match; main exits with that code (0/1). Terminal.Loop and buffered Matcher.scan are bypassed. Input bytes, environment defaults, configured callbacks/algorithm selection and OS I/O are dynamic boundaries; this is source reconstruction, not a measured execution trace.

The evidenced direct production consumer is fzf.Run, with two call sites: asynchronous ingestion for non-streaming execution and synchronous streaming-filter ingestion. Thus both interactive/buffered-filter and streaming-filter paths depend on ReadSource. A change could affect ingestion/source selection/readiness/completion, but actual behavioral impact depends on the change; no regression was executed. main is only transitive. Lattice returned zero incoming calls even with includeEstimated=true, so that result is incomplete rather than evidence of no consumers.

test/test_filter.rb defines noninteractive TestFilter tests. test_filter_exitstatus loops over ordinary filtering and --no-sort: echo foo filtered by foo must print foo and exit 0; filtering by bar must print nothing and exit 1. test_default_extended and test_exact exercise query semantics. These are Ruby subprocess tests: FZF in test/lib/common.rb points to repository bin/fzf with explicit environment options; shell backticks pipe data to that executable, entering main→ParseOptions→Run. test/runner.rb loads test_*.rb and Minitest autorun. Tests were inspected, not run; the Ruby-to-Go process edge is source-supported, not a resolved map call edge.

The query arrives as CLI argv after the executable name. ParseOptions starts from defaults, optionally parses FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS_FILE and FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS, then CLI arguments. parseOptions handles -f/--filter via nextString and stores a *string in Options.Filter; missing text is an error. This is separate from Options.Query. Run converts *Filter to []rune for patternBuilder→BuildPattern and optionally prints the original filter. BuildPattern trims surrounding unescaped spaces in extended mode, consults its cache and parseTerms; terms receive case handling, normalization and extended operators. With default foo, this becomes a non-inverse fuzzy term. Matching consumes the resulting Pattern.
